To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a new method to model the tumor volume change in response to radio‐therapy in HN cancer patients.

a novel technique was developed for the modeling of tumor shrinkage/growths in head‐and‐neck cancer in response to radio‐therapy to better understand the treatment process and to compute the cumulative dose distribution for adaptive radiation therapy.
we developed an image feature based tumor shrinkage model for HN cancer for adaptive radiation therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) development of an image feature based tumor shrinkage modeling technique for HN cancer, (2) application of the new technique for adaptive radiation therapy, and (3) investigation of the clinical utility of the new technique.
the development of a model to predict the tumor response to RT in HN cancer, and to use it in ART.
the development of novel image processing algorithms for the modeling of the tumor shrinkage in HN cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the image feature‐based modeling of tumor response to radio‐therapy is feasible and promising.
we have developed an image feature based model to derive the kinetics of the tumor response to radiation.
we developed an image feature based method to model tumor response in HN cancer to radiotherapy for ART.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model could be used as a tool to predict the tumor response to radiation therapy and provide a basis for adaptive radiation therapy.
the tumor response to radiation is a dynamic process.
the tumor response to radiation can be modeled accurately using image features and the model can be used to guide ART.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tumor response to radiation is not linear, but rather nonlinear.
